summary: Stepping back to synthesize the broader picture, today’s market action marks an inflection in the regime divergence we have tracked all month. For weeks, risk assets leaned into a pristine Goldilocks assumption that corporate margins were bulletproof against elevated capital costs. The Warsh Fed has effectively shattered that assumption by restarting the hiking cycle.

Stepping back to synthesize the broader picture, the tension defining the session is an asset class standoff. Equities and credit are acting on the assumption that nominal G.D.P. growth and robust corporate earnings will outrun the Fed’s tightening cycle. But that thesis hinges on capital costs remaining merely restrictive, rather than actively suffocating.
